meta.head: feat/rate-limit
meta.title: Token-bucket rate limiting for the public API
meta.summary: The change adds a token-bucket rate limiter and applies it to every public route. Buckets are kept per API key in memory, refill at a fixed rate, and reject over-limit requests with HTTP 429.

chapters.title: Overview
chapters.narration: This change adds per-key rate limiting to the public API. A new token-bucket module backs a request middleware that returns 429 when a key runs dry.

chapters.title: The TokenBucket type
chapters.narration: TokenBucket holds a capacity, a refill rate, and a timestamp. Each take refills it by elapsed time, then spends one token if one is available.

chapters.title: Per-key bucket registry
chapters.narration: RateLimiter maps each API key to its own bucket, created on first sight. A lock guards the plain dict, sized for one process.

chapters.title: Wiring into the middleware
chapters.narration: The middleware reads the API key header and asks the limiter for a token. A rejection short-circuits with 429 and a Retry-After header.

chapters.title: Tests
chapters.narration: The tests freeze time to check refill arithmetic, exhaust a bucket to hit the 429 path, and confirm distinct keys use distinct buckets.

chapters.title: Wrap-up
chapters.narration: Per-key limits now live in one module, wired through a single middleware and covered by time-controlled tests.
